definitions.explanation: An expression of sympathy offered to someone who has lost a loved one. The お prefix makes it polite. Used both as a noun and in set phrases when offering condolences.

examples.japanese: お{悔|く}やみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧。
⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{悔|く}やみ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: I wrote a letter of condolence to my friend's family.

examples.japanese: ⟦{突然|とつぜん}→突然：00409_totsuzen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{訃報|ふほう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{接|せっ}し→接する：12920_sessuru⟧、⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧お{悔|く}やみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧。
examples.english: Upon receiving the sudden news of the passing, I offer my heartfelt condolences.

notes:
REGISTER:
お{悔|く}やみ is inherently polite due to the お prefix. The most common set phrase is お{悔|く}やみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧, a formal expression used at funerals and in writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{悔|く}やみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げる→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧ (to offer condolences — formal)
- お{悔|く}やみ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧ (words of condolence)
- お{悔|く}やみ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧ (condolence letter)
- お{悔|く}やみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{述|の}べる→述べる：02389_noberu⟧ (to express condolences)
